title: Evaluating and Mitigating LLM-as-a-judge Bias in Communication Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Injecting unnecessary elaboration, extensive context, or flowery language into clean Q&A answers using GPT-4o, and measuring how point-wise scores from LLM judges change compared to concise answers.
Iteratively lengthening answers without adding new semantic value to evaluate if LLM judges assign higher scores simply based on response volume.
Formatting answers with explicit, step-by-step reasoning processes to test whether judges preferentially score them differently than direct conclusions.
Modifying the emotional tone of answers to be overly positive, polite, or empathetic to assess if LLM judges confuse emotional wording with higher answer quality.
Introducing formal citations or references to expert sources (even if fabricated or irrelevant) to test if judges over-rely on authority cues.
Injecting subtle factual mistakes into confidently phrased answers to determine if LLM judges fail to penalize incorrect content.
Adding cues regarding the responder's demographic group or gender into the text to observe if LLM judges alter their scores based on ingrained stereotypes or identity representations.
Aligning answers with majority opinions or stating that 'most people think X' to evaluate if judges give extra credit for perceived consensus.
Adding off-topic facts, extraneous anecdotes, or unrelated descriptions to see if judges are subconsciously impressed and reward the distracted content.
Attributing identical answers to different sources (e.g., a reputed AI model vs. an unknown model) to test if judges unfairly score based on the perceived reputation of the author.
